snippet.title: The Psychology of People Who Easily Forget Names
snippet.description:
The Psychology of People Who Easily Forget Names

Have you ever met someone, heard their name, and forgotten it five seconds later? It’s a frustrating experience that happens to the best of us. But here’s the truth: forgetting names isn’t actually about a bad memory. In this video, we explore the deep psychological reasons why our brains filter out names during social interactions. We discuss the paradox of social anxiety, the difference between abstract data and meaningful stories, and how the pressure to perform in conversation blocks our ability to absorb information. Discover how to stop forgetting names by shifting your focus from yourself to the person in front of you. If you’ve ever felt embarrassed by a memory slip, this deep dive into human behavior and cognitive psychology will change how you see every conversation.

snippet.title: The Psychology of Being The Black Sheep.
snippet.description:
The Psychology of Being The Black Sheep. 

Most people assume criticism hurts less when it comes from those closest to us because they know us best. Social psychology suggests the opposite can happen. When someone breaks the unwritten rules of a family, friend group, community, or team, they are often judged more harshly than a complete outsider. This is known as the black sheep phenomenon. The reason is uncomfortable but deeply human. We attach part of our identity to the groups we belong to, and when a member behaves in a way that threatens that identity, it feels personal. The group reacts not only to the behavior itself but also to what it believes that behavior says about everyone connected to it. Sometimes the people who know you best become the people who punish difference the most.

snippet.title: Trailer | A Social Life | A Short Film By Kerith lemon
snippet.description:
A Social Life is the story of Meredith, a career focused young woman who understands the importance of keeping up an active social media profile. She strives to live a balanced life: staying fit, working hard and connecting with friends. Sharing these moments online is an important part of her day-to-day; she is creating her "image" within her broader social media friend base. 

Meredith awakes one day and realizes that her reflection is merely the collection of photos that she has shared with others. Is this her life? Or just a carefully curated brand? 

A Social Life seeks to ask the question, “are we truly living the life that we post?” Whether we are, or are not, we want to discuss what effect does this have on one’s self-esteem and that of our extended community.

snippet.title: Inside the Mind of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei | Full documentary | 4K
snippet.description:
Inside the Mind of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei - Emily Chang sits down with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in a wide-ranging interview discussing his San Francisco roots, the race against OpenAI, the Pentagon standoff and AI’s endgame.

Inside the Mind of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei  (2026)

Artificial intelligence is advancing faster than almost anyone predicted.

At the center of this transformation stands Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic and one of the most influential voices shaping the future of AI.

In this exclusive interview with Emily Chang, Amodei reflects on his journey from growing up in San Francisco to leading one of the world's most important AI companies.

The conversation explores Anthropic's rivalry with OpenAI, the competition to build increasingly powerful AI systems, and the difficult decisions facing the industry as artificial intelligence moves from research labs into every part of society.

Amodei discusses the growing relationship between AI companies and governments, including tensions surrounding national security, defense applications and the Pentagon's role in the development of advanced artificial intelligence.

The interview also tackles some of the biggest questions of our time.

How powerful will AI become?

Can humanity maintain control over increasingly capable systems?

Will artificial intelligence create unprecedented prosperity or introduce risks we are not prepared to manage?

From AI safety and regulation to the race for technological leadership, this conversation offers a rare look into the thinking of one of the architects of the AI era.

Because the future of artificial intelligence may not be decided by technology alone.

It may be decided by the people building it.

snippet.title: Parents Took an Exam And Got to Know What Kids Feel.
snippet.description:
Parents Took an Exam And Got to Know What Kids Feel.

The Cello Exam Expert campaign by JWT Mumbai created a powerful role-reversal scenario where parents attending what they believed was a regular parent-teacher meeting were unexpectedly given their child’s 6th-grade mid-term exam. What started as a routine interaction quickly turned into discomfort, confusion, and realization as the parents struggled to answer questions they assumed would be simple. The emotional impact of the campaign came from this reversal of perspective, allowing adults to directly experience the pressure children face during exams. Instead of telling parents about academic stress, it made them feel it in real time. The result was a deeper understanding of how expectations, pressure, and performance affect students in everyday school environments.

snippet.title: Nikola Tesla - The visionary who invented our future | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Nikola Tesla, born in 1856 in what is now Croatia, was one of the world’s greatest inventors. He developed numerous innovations in the field of electrical engineering and was granted over 280 patents, many of them in the USA.

Nikola Tesla arrived in New York in 1884 with barely a cent to his name. He worked briefly for Thomas Alva Edison, the inventor of the light bulb. However, their collaboration soon ended in a dispute. In the years that followed, Tesla developed groundbreaking technologies and implemented alternating current systems for the Westinghouse company. These shaped modern electrification.

For decades, Tesla conducted research into high-frequency alternating currents and the vision of wireless power transmission - a concept that was far ahead of its time. He also recognized early on that solar energy would become one of the most important sources of energy in the future. However, his visionary inventions were not fully realized during his lifetime.

Tesla’s life was marked by extremes: periods of abject poverty and professional setbacks alternated with an eccentric lifestyle that’s been heavily mythologized. In 1943, he died alone and destitute in a New York hotel.

localized.title: Nikola Tesla - The visionary who invented our future | DW Documentary
localized.description:
Nikola Tesla, born in 1856 in what is now Croatia, was one of the world’s greatest inventors. He developed numerous innovations in the field of electrical engineering and was granted over 280 patents, many of them in the USA.

Nikola Tesla arrived in New York in 1884 with barely a cent to his name. He worked briefly for Thomas Alva Edison, the inventor of the light bulb. However, their collaboration soon ended in a dispute. In the years that followed, Tesla developed groundbreaking technologies and implemented alternating current systems for the Westinghouse company. These shaped modern electrification.

For decades, Tesla conducted research into high-frequency alternating currents and the vision of wireless power transmission - a concept that was far ahead of its time. He also recognized early on that solar energy would become one of the most important sources of energy in the future. However, his visionary inventions were not fully realized during his lifetime.

Tesla’s life was marked by extremes: periods of abject poverty and professional setbacks alternated with an eccentric lifestyle that’s been heavily mythologized. In 1943, he died alone and destitute in a New York hotel.

Discover why your worth isn't tied to what you can do for others, but who you are as a human being. It is time to stop losing yourself in the process of helping everyone else.

snippet.title: Ecouter la maladie quand elle murmure et non plus quand elle crie | Agnès MARTINEC | TEDxSaclay
snippet.description: Et si la solution n’était pas de mieux voir la tumeur, mais de détecter la maladie avant qu’elle ne devienne visible ? Directrice des Opérations et cofondatrice associée de CYBERNA, elle accompagne la structuration et le développement de solutions innovantes, notamment pour la détection ultra-précoce des cancers. snippet.title: Your Childhood Shapes Your Entire Life Till The End
snippet.description:
Your Childhood Shapes Your Entire Life Till The End

There's a quiet moment in adulthood where you realize your reactions—the way you avoid conflict, the need to over-apologize, the inability to rest—aren't driven by your adult self, but by the child you once were. This video explores the profound, often invisible, way our earliest years create the emotional blueprint for our entire lives. We dive deep into the psychology of how childhood survival strategies become adult emotional patterns, shaping everything from our relationships and self-worth to our ambitions and fears. If you've ever wondered why certain things feel heavier than they should, why rejection hurts so intensely, or why you struggle to trust—this is the conversation you need. We explore the roles we adopted (the peacemaker, the performer, the observer) and how to shift from being controlled by the past to using awareness as a tool for healing and growth. Your childhood is your origin, but it is not your destiny. The power to rewrite your script begins with understanding where it started. Watch now to start understanding your emotional defaults and begin the journey of becoming the adult you always needed.

snippet.title: #Foodporn Doesn't Cook Itself | A Social Life Film | Teaser
snippet.description:
Are you living the life that you post?

A Social Life is a short film about a career driven woman named Meredith who's living the life she's always dreamed of... online. Meredith strives to live a balanced life: staying fit, working hard and connecting with her friends; she is creating her "image" within her broader social media friend base. But she awakes one day and realizes that her reflection is merely the collection of photos that she has shared with others. Is this her life? Or just a carefully curated brand?

Cast: Rosalind Ross & Lani Hall Alpert

Kerith Lemon is a writer, director and creator with rich experience in multi-platform storytelling and creative narratives. Driven by her passion for stories that emotionally connect, Lemon is drawn to narratives that elevate women, mirror societal complications, and create dialogues amongst a broad audience. Her directorial debut, A Social Life, premiered at the Canberra International Short Film Festival, where it was awarded the prize for Best International Actor and most recently has won Best Ladies First Short at the Lady Filmmakers Festival in Pacific Grove, CA. It will continue to screen at film festivals throughout 2016.
